:::{#sol-prac-exp-mle-ci .solution}

By @sol-prac-exp-mle-oinf-at-mle,
$\SE{\hat\pmean_{ML}} \approx \sqrt{I(\hat\pmean_{ML}; \vx)^{-1}} = \frac{\bar{x}}{\sqrt{n}}$.
An [approximate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#def-approximate-ci) 95% CI for $\pmean$ is:

$$
\hat\pmean_{ML} \pm 1.96 \times \frac{\bar{x}}{\sqrt{n}}
= \bar{x} \pm \frac{1.96\bar{x}}{\sqrt{n}}
$$

Note: the exponential distribution has $\Varf{X} = \pmean^2$,
so $\SE{\hat\pmean_{ML}} = \pmean/\sqrt{n}$,
which is estimated by $\bar{x}/\sqrt{n}$.
More generally,
the standard error of a sample mean is $\SD{X}/\sqrt{n}$;
here that reduces to $\pmean/\sqrt{n}$
because $\SD{X} = \pmean$ for the exponential distribution.

:::
